name: AZNO Foot & Ankle Specialist
what_they_do: Podiatry practice of Dr. Nadia Shah, DPM (New York College of Podiatric Medicine, three-year reconstructive foot and ankle surgical residency at Hoboken University Medical Center), providing primary foot care, conditions treatment and surgery for central New Jersey from one East Brunswick office.
customers: Local adults with foot and ankle pain, sports and diabetic foot issues; a very large existing patient base judging by review volume, plus insurance-referred patients.

size_signals.signal: One provider and one office (172 Summerhill Rd, Ste 2) with long hours: Mon-Fri 8am-7pm, Sat 8am-2pm, Sunday by appointment
~1,323 Google reviews at 4.8, plus 255 reviews at 4.88 on Zocdoc - inference: high patient throughput for a single-provider office
Website built by a healthcare marketing agency (Jet Digital) with sitemap, blog and review-request tooling

website_review.primary_cta: 'BOOK ONLINE' in the nav and multiple 'Request An Appointment Today' buttons, plus an accessibility bar with 'Call Us' and 'Text Us'
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Yes - BOOK ONLINE leads to a Tebra (ex-Kareo) booking profile where a patient picks Dr. Shah and available times; the on-site contact form is a Gravity Form protected by Google reCAPTCHA
website_review.trust_signals: Provider bio with training detail, review-request and 'what can we improve' links, patient-education pages, insurance page, map link, accessibility tools
website_review.out_of_date_signs: A cookie-consent dialog covers the bottom half of the phone screen on first load; the home page carries no hours or address above the fold (they only appear on Contact); structured data stops at WebPage/WebSite
website_review.search_basics: Good: title is 'Podiatrist in East Brunswick, NJ | Azno Foot & Ankle Specialist', meta description names the town and the request-appointment action, and SERVICES, Conditions Treated, New Patients, Providers and Contact each have their own page
top_issues: No LocalBusiness/Physician schema - only generic WebPage/WebSite/ReadAction nodes, so hours and address are not machine-readable
Contact form gated by Google reCAPTCHA, blocking automated/AI-assisted enquiries
Hours do not appear on the home page and the Sunday 'by appointments only' line is vague
Cookie-consent overlay takes over the mobile screen before any content is read

agent_readiness.notes: Findable: crawlable WordPress site with a sitemap index and by far the strongest review profile in the batch (~1,300 reviews at 4.8), but no LocalBusiness schema. Answerable: address, phone, hours, email and services are all real text on the Contact and Services pages (home page has no hours), yet the JSON-LD only declares WebPage/WebSite. Bookable: genuinely good - BOOK ONLINE hands off to a Tebra booking profile with provider and time selection and no phone call, though the site's own contact form sits behind a reCAPTCHA.

operations_signals.signal: Separate 'Text Us' channel plus 'what can we improve' feedback page - inference: the practice already runs multi-channel patient messaging and has no unified inbox we could see
Single provider covering Mon-Fri 8am-7pm plus Saturday mornings, with ~1,300 reviews implying heavy volume - inference: front desk triage and rescheduling load is the constraint
Contact form still asks patients to avoid sending health information, pushing clinical questions back to the phone

top_opportunities.opportunity: Add full Physician/LocalBusiness schema (address, hours incl. the Sunday-by-appointment rule, provider, services) so agents can answer 'are you open, where, who, what do you treat' without scraping
top_opportunities.evidence: ld+json on the site contains only WebPage, WebSite, ReadAction, BreadcrumbList and SearchAction types - no LocalBusiness or Physician

top_opportunities.opportunity: Replace the reCAPTCHA-gated contact form with an agent-submittable intake that captures reason for visit and insurance, and route it into the same queue as the Tebra bookings
top_opportunities.evidence: Contact form includes a g-recaptcha-response field and instructs patients not to describe their problem

top_opportunities.opportunity: Use the huge review base as a growth asset: put reviews on the site, add FAQ answers built from what reviewers ask, and automate post-visit review requests to keep 4.8 momentum
top_opportunities.evidence: ~1,323 Google reviews at 4.8 exist but the site shows no review content or ratings on the pages I checked

scores.reasons: Gap: small - this is the most mature site in the batch (agency-built, page-per-service, real Tebra booking, big review base); what is missing is schema, an unblocked form and on-page proof. Pay: high review volume implies a busy, profitable practice that can afford work. Ease: schema plus form changes are days of work. Evidence: I verified the schema types, the booking redirect to Tebra, the reCAPTCHA and the mobile cookie overlay myself; review figures come from aggregators.
